step1.title: Sentences & gaps
step1.lede: Write each sentence the way it reads when it is solved, then click the word that becomes the gap. The words you gap fill the word bank by themselves — you never type an answer twice.
step1.tipTitle: Two ways to make a gap.
step1.tipBody: Click a word in the strip under a sentence — or put square brackets around it while you write:
step1.summary: {sentences, plural, one {# sentence} other {# sentences}} · {gaps, plural, one {# gap} other {# gaps}}
step1.emptyBody: Add the first sentence, or paste a whole set at once and mark the gaps afterwards.
step1.sentencePlaceholder: Write the full sentence, with the correct word in place…
step1.tokensLabel: Click a word to turn it into a gap
step1.tokenMakeGap: Click to make this a gap
step1.tokensHelpMark: Click the word students should fill in.
step1.tokensHelpRemove: Click a highlighted word to remove the gap.
step1.errorEmpty: Write the sentence, or delete this card.
step1.errorNoGap: Mark at least one word as a gap.
step1.hintHelp: Shown under the sentence before they answer. Use it for context, not for the answer.
step1.pasteHelp: One sentence per line. Square brackets around a word mark it as a gap.

step2.title: Word bank
step2.lede: Decide how students supply the word: pick it from a shared bank, or type it. With a bank, the correct answers come from your sentences — you only add the wrong words.
step2.modeBankHelp: One strip of words serves every sentence. Words you add here are the wrong ones.
step2.modeFreeHelp: No bank is shown. Students type into the gap, so the only thing to decide is which spellings you accept.
step2.answersHelp: Taken from the words you gapped in step 1. Change them there — never here.
step2.answersEmpty: No gaps yet. Mark a word in step 1 and it appears here.
step2.reuseHint: {words} answers more than one gap. Turn on “A word can fill several gaps”, or those gaps cannot all be solved.
step2.distractorsHelp: Shown in the bank beside the answers. Enter adds one; separate several with commas.
step2.bankOk: {bankSize} words for {gapCount, plural, one {# gap} other {# gaps}} — enough that the last gaps are still a choice.
step2.bankTooSmall: {bankSize} words for {gapCount, plural, one {# gap} other {# gaps}}: the last gaps solve themselves by elimination. Add a couple of wrong words.
step2.shuffleHelp: A different order for every student and every attempt.
step2.allowReuse: A word can fill several gaps
step2.allowReuseHelp: Off, a word is spent once it is placed — which is half of what the exercise teaches.
step2.showBankCount: Show how many words are left
step2.showBankCountHelp: A count above the bank while they work.
step2.checkingLocked: One check for the whole exercise
step2.checkingLockedHelp: Not a setting: students check everything at once, as often as they like.
step2.alternativesHelp: The word in the sentence is always accepted. Add other forms you would also mark right, separated by commas.
step2.pairsUnused: {count, plural, one {# word-specific explanation} other {# word-specific explanations}} will not be shown: they explain a word that was chosen, and here students type.

step1.title: What kind of correction is this?
step1.lede: You never type the mistakes in as a list. You write the sentence the way the student meets it, and the sentence the way it should be — the builder works out what separates them, and that becomes the mistakes to find.

modeHelp.sentences: One mistake per sentence is the norm.
modeHelp.passage: Three to five mistakes in one paragraph.

step1.sentencesNote: Each sentence stands on its own. Students can correct them in any order.
step1.passageNote: The whole paragraph is one submission. Students are not told which sentence holds the mistake.
step1.passageManyItems: {count, plural, one {# text block here} other {# text blocks here}} — a continuous text is usually one.
step1.instructionsPlaceholder: Finn feilen i hver setning og skriv den riktig.
step1.instructionsHelp: One line, in the language students are learning. Required — an exercise without it cannot be published.
step1.notePlaceholder: Where the sentences come from, or what to look out for.
step1.noteHelp: Shown under the task line, before students start.
step1.tip: Build the mistakes out of sentences your students have actually written. Invented mistakes tend to be either too easy to spot, or so wrong that nobody recognises them.

step2.title: The sentences and the answer key
step2.titlePassage: The text and the answer key
step2.lede: Two lines per task. The builder compares them word by word and shows you what it has turned into a mistake — check that the list matches what you actually want to test.
step2.refRequired: Without an answer key there are no mistakes.
step2.errorsHere: {count, plural, one {# mistake to find} other {# mistakes to find}}
step2.identical: The two lines are the same. The student would have nothing to correct.
step2.acceptBothHelp: Accept both forms — then this is not a mistake the student has to find.
step2.spanNotePlaceholder: Why is this wrong? Shown to the student after grading.
step2.altsHelp: One whole sentence per line. Write (liker|elsker) for variants inside a line.
step2.hintPlaceholder: What happens to the verb when the sentence starts with a time expression?
step2.hintHelp: The student chooses whether to open it.
step2.teacherNotePlaceholder: The V2 rule — came up on the last test.
step2.teacherNoteHelp: Shown in the grading queue, never to the student.

step3.title: What does the student know, and what does the machine accept?
step3.lede: Error correction is easy to make impossible. The number of mistakes is the one piece of information that decides whether this is an exercise or a guessing game — the rest is tuning how strictly the text is read.
step3.countLabel: Show how many mistakes there are
step3.countHelp: “{count} mistakes to find” stands at the top. Without it the student does not know when they are done.
step3.markLabel: Mark the sentences that hold a mistake
step3.markHelp: The student sees which sentences are affected, but not which word.
step3.hintTextHelp: The hint you wrote in step 2 sits behind a button; the student chooses.
step3.noHintsWritten: No hints written yet — add one to a sentence in step 2 and this can be switched on.
step3.showTypeHelp: “Word form” stands beside it. Makes the task markedly easier — usually A2 only.
step3.onHelp: Compares the student's sentence with your answer key, word by word.
step3.exactPassLabel: A hit on the answer key is approved without a teacher
step3.exactPassHelp: Every mistake corrected and nothing else changed. Everything else joins the queue.
step3.requireAllSpansLabel: Require every mistake to have been touched
step3.requireAllSpansHelp: One untouched mistake stops automatic approval, even if the rest is right.
step3.nothingApproved: Nothing is approved automatically while a hit on the answer key still goes to the teacher.
step3.typoHelp: “leiligheten” against “leilgheten” counts as a hit in long words.
step3.caseHelp: Only turn this on if a capital is never the point here.
step3.punctHelp: Cannot be on if a comma or a full stop is one of the mistakes.

strayHelp.ignore: Only the answer key counts. A rewritten but correct sentence can be approved.
strayHelp.flag: The answer can still be approved, but the teacher sees what else was touched.
strayHelp.block: Touch anything outside the mistakes and the answer always goes to the teacher.

step3.nearHelp: An answer that fixed no mistake is still called partly corrected from {percent}% similarity to the answer key.
step3.offWarning: With no automatic check every single answer lands in the teacher's queue untouched — the correct ones included.

step4.title: The road from handing in to a mark
step4.lede: The automatic check can only approve. Everything it does not settle, and everything it is unsure about, ends up with you.
step4.stageStudentChecks: {count, plural, one {# self-check before handing in} other {# self-checks before handing in}}
step4.stageStudentBlind: No self-check — they hand in blind
step4.stageCheckOn: Compares against the answer key, word by word
step4.stageTeacherDetail: Sees everything that was not approved automatically
step4.selfCheckOn: The student learns how many mistakes are corrected — never which words are left.
step4.showSpanCountLabel: Show how many are corrected in the self-check
step4.showSpanCountHelp: “2 of 3 corrected”, with a dot per mistake. Without it the student gets a general message only.
step4.noSelfCheck: There is no self-check to show it in — allow at least one above.
step4.keyboardHelp: Extra keys in the editing field.
step4.showRefsLabel: When is the answer key shown?

showRefsHelp.afterGraded: The answer key comes with the teacher's feedback.
showRefsHelp.afterSubmit: The student sees it at once — which makes another attempt worth little.
showRefsHelp.never: The student never sees the answer key, only whether the correction was right.

spanTypeHelp.form: The right word, inflected wrongly — tense, definiteness, number.
spanTypeHelp.order: The right words in the wrong order.
spanTypeHelp.extra: A word that should not be there at all.
spanTypeHelp.missing: A word the sentence needs and does not have.
spanTypeHelp.function: A small word carrying grammar: a preposition, an article, a conjunction.

tester.title: Try it as a student
tester.howTo: Correct it here and you will see the verdict a student would get, and whether it would reach you at all.
tester.diffLabel: The sentence against the answer key

issues.EX_NO_INSTRUCTION: No task line yet — students open the exercise without being told what to do.
issues.PASSAGE_MANY_ITEMS: {count, plural, one {# text block} other {# text blocks}} in a continuous text — students submit all of them as one.
issues.EX_NO_ITEMS: Nothing to correct yet. Write a sentence with a mistake and its answer key.
issues.ITEM_NO_REF: Sentence {index}: no answer key, so there is no mistake to find.
issues.ITEM_IDENTICAL: Sentence {index}: the two lines are identical — the student would have nothing to correct.
issues.ITEM_ALL_SOFT: Sentence {index}: every difference is accepted as an alternative, so nothing counts as a mistake.
issues.ITEM_MANY_ERRORS: Sentence {index} holds {count, plural, one {# mistake} other {# mistakes}} — heavy for one task.
issues.ITEM_TOO_LONG: Sentence {index} is {count, plural, one {# word} other {# words}} long. Finding a mistake turns into reading.
issues.SPAN_ORDER_TOO_WIDE: Sentence {index}: a word-order mistake spanning {count, plural, one {# word} other {# words}} leaves the student unsure where it starts.
issues.ITEM_ALT_EQUALS_WRONG: Sentence {index}: one of the accepted alternatives is the faulty sentence itself.
issues.ITEM_COUNT_HIDDEN: Sentence {index} holds {count, plural, one {# mistake} other {# mistakes}}, and the number is hidden — that makes it guesswork.
issues.CHECK_IGNORE_PUNCT: Punctuation is ignored, so a comma or a full stop cannot be one of the mistakes.
issues.CHECK_CASE_INSENSITIVE: Capital letters are ignored, so a capital cannot be one of the mistakes.
issues.CHECK_STRAY_IGNORED: Changes outside the mistakes are ignored — a rewritten but correct sentence can pass.
issues.CHECK_NEAR_TOO_LOW: “Partly corrected” starts at {percent}% similarity, which is low enough to flatter a wrong answer.
issues.HINT_TYPE_WITHOUT_COUNT: The type of each mistake is shown, but not how many there are.
issues.AI_WITHOUT_CHECK: The AI stage is on while the automatic check is off.
issues.AI_UNLIMITED_BEFORE_SUBMIT: Students see the AI comment before submitting, with no limit on self-checks.
issues.REFS_AFTER_SUBMIT_WITH_RETRIES: The answer key is shown right after submitting, which makes another attempt worth little.

step1.title: Which way round?
step1.lede: The direction decides which language the sentence is read in, and which one the answer key is written in.
step1.flowHelp: Every accepted translation you write in step 2 has to be in {writes}.
step1.flowBothHelp: Each sentence carries its own direction, set on its card in step 2.
step1.singleManyItems: {count} sentences are written, and only the first will be shown. Nothing is deleted — switch back to a set to use them again.
step1.instructionsHelp: The one line the student reads first.
step1.noteHelp: Shown above the sentences, before the work is handed in.
step1.tip: The auto-check can only approve an answer that matches your key. Everything else goes to a teacher — which is why writing several accepted translations per sentence is the single most useful thing you can do here.

step2.title: The sentences and their translations
step2.lede: One card per sentence: what the student reads, and every translation that counts as right.
step2.coverage: {multi} of {total} sentences accept more than one wording
step2.refPlaceholder: Jeg (har bodd|bodde) i Tromsø i tre år.
step2.altsSyntax: Write alternatives inline: (liker|elsker) accepts either, (nå|) makes the word optional.
step2.variantCount: {count, plural, one {# variant accepted} other {# variants accepted}}
step2.hintHelp: The student opens it themselves, before answering.
step2.glossHelp: Shown under the sentence while the student writes. Press Enter to add.
step2.explanationLabel: Why the key reads this way
step2.explanationPlaceholder: The time expression comes first, so the verb stays in second place.
step2.explanationHelp: Shown with the answer key. The check can never say why a translation is wrong — this is where that comes from.
step2.teacherNoteHelp: Only ever shown in the review queue. The student never sees it.
step2.audioNotForDirection: The sentence is read in {lang} — there is nothing here worth voicing. Turn the direction round to build a listening task.
step2.audioInvalidType: That file is not an audio format the platform accepts.
step2.audioTooLarge: The recording is larger than 100 MB.

step3.title: What the check accepts
step3.lede: The check compares an answer with your accepted translations, word by word. It can approve a hit — it cannot decide that a different wording is also right, so everything else goes to you with a diff.
step3.onHelp: Off means every answer reaches you untouched.
step3.offWarning: With the check off nothing is approved automatically — every sentence of every submission waits for you.
step3.exactPassLabel: A hit on the key closes without a teacher
step3.exactPassHelp: Saves you the answers there is nothing to judge in. Turn it off if everything should pass your desk.

route.typo: One letter off, in one word

routeHelp.exact: After normalisation: the same words in the same order.
routeHelp.typo: The student sees which word; you decide whether it counts.
routeHelp.near: This is what sorts your queue — nearly-right answers go quickly.
routeHelp.off: May well be a different, perfectly good translation. Only a person can tell.

step3.normLede: What should not count as a mistake before the answer is compared.
step3.punctHelp: Full stops, commas and quotation marks are dropped.
step3.typoLabel: Allow one letter's slip per word
step3.typoHelp: «Tromso» against «Tromsø» becomes a spelling slip, not a different word. Words shorter than four letters are never forgiven this way.
step3.foldLabel: æ, ø, å count as a, o, a
step3.foldHelp: For students without a Norwegian keyboard.
step3.foldWarning: This hides real spelling mistakes: «bla» now passes for «blå».
step3.nearHelp: {percent}% of the words shared with the closest accepted translation. Above it, the answer sorts to the front of your queue.
step3.guardsLede: When the task trains one thing — the perfect tense, word order — you can require or forbid a form. A guard that fires is the only thing the check may call wrong outright, so write down why it is wrong.
step3.guardsNoItems: Write the sentences in step 2 first — requirements are attached to them.
step3.guardsExplained: {explained} of {total} requirements have an explanation for the student.
step3.guardNotePlaceholder: The task asks for the perfect tense.
step3.coverageCallout: The check only knows your key. {multi} of {total} sentences accept more than one wording — the rest will often flag a correct answer as «close». Write down the variants you know of, and let the rest come to you.

step4.title: The road to a mark
step4.lede: Three stages before you, and you at the end. Only the first and the last exist today.
step4.stageCheckOn: Diffs against your key. Approves a clean hit, sorts the rest.
step4.stageCheckNoPass: Diffs against your key and sorts the rest — approving nothing, by your setting.
step4.stageCheckOff: Off — nothing is judged before you see it.
step4.stageAiDetail: Would weigh whether a different wording is also right, and draft a comment.
step4.stageTeacherDetail: Sets the verdict. Can approve, comment or send back.
step4.aiHelp: Reserves its place in the queue and the fields it will fill. The model itself comes later.
step4.aiChecksLabel: What the AI should look at

aiHelpFor.order: Inversion and subordinate clauses — what translations trip on most.
aiHelpFor.lexis: Whether another word than the key's also carries the meaning.

step4.aiVisibilityHelp: The student never sees a mark from the AI, only remarks.
step4.keyboardHelp: For keyboards without the Norwegian letters.
step4.glossHelp: The glosses you wrote in step 2.
step4.noGlossWritten: No glosses written yet — add them to a sentence in step 2.
step4.selfCheckOn: Each self-check shows the diff against the key with the missing words hidden behind •••.
step4.selfCheckOff: The student hands in without ever seeing how close they are.

attemptsHelp.free: The student may correct and hand in again, feedback included.
attemptsHelp.once: Locked after handing in — only a teacher can reopen it.

showRefsHelp.afterSubmit: The student sees the key while the answer waits in your queue.

showRefsHelp.never: The key stays between you and the other teachers.
